messages:
jose: Quick sync after the RFC. Proposal: split dashboard requests into hot (precomputed tiles via edge cache) and cold (query-service). Main debate left: do we enforce RBAC at the edge so cached hits stay fast, or keep all auth in the query-service to avoid divergence?

tara: Numbers pls. rough latency impact on hot path if we move auth to service?

jose: Benchmarks today: tile served from edge ~25ms total. If edge skips auth and every hit goes to service for auth, p50 becomes ~40ms, p95 ~260ms for cold falls. If edge runs a quick check (signed token verify) we can keep ~28-32ms p95 on hot hits.

kevin: Signed tokens at edge sound promising. How do we avoid staleness when perms change?

jose: Use short-lived perm tokens issued by auth, include a monotonic revocation sequence. Edge keys verify HMAC locally. Cache key becomes (tile-id, perm-seq). When seq increments, cache miss forces cold validation.

mira: Implementation sketch: auth-service issues token: `perm:v3:role=analyst;seq=987;exp=1700000000;sig=...` Edge verifies sig and seq. Query-service always re-checks on cold path.

tara: HMAC verify is cheap but at 20k rps it adds up. Need cost estimate + ops ramifications (key rotation, key distribution).

kevin: Suggest lightweight rust verifier in edge binary, keyring refreshed via control-plane streaming. Rotate keys infrequently, but revocations use seq bump. Also add a fast cache for recently verified tokens at edge (ttl ~5s) to reduce CPU thrash.

jose: Rollout plan: 1) metrics baseline collection 2) deploy token issuance + edge verify in canary (2%) 3) ramp to 20% then 100%, with automated rollback if hit-rate drops or auth_err spikes 4) enable shard-level eviction quotas to reduce tenant hot spots.

mira: What metrics/traces do we need? I propose: tags: `lane=hot|cold`, `auth=edge|service`, `perm_seq`, `tile_id`, `tenant`. Counters: `tile_requests`, `tile_cache_hits`, `tile_auth_failures`. Histograms: `edge_verify_ms`, `service_auth_ms`, `tile_end2end_ms`.

kevin: Also add alerting: if cache-hit-rate drops > 8% within 10m of a rollout step or auth_failures increase > 3x baseline, auto rollback.

tara: Security question: could a leaked perm token allow amplification (replay) to fetch many tiles? Mitigation: bind token to session id + short TTL + per-token rate limit on edge.

security-bot: Security review required for token format and replay mitigations before canary. Please list proof points: HMAC algo, key storage, TTL, binding fields.

jose: Will add to follow-up doc. Also adding chaos test: flip a user's role and assert their cached tiles are invalidated within 2x TTL. Add this to CI perf suite.

kevin: One more ops detail: consistent hashing must include `perm_seq` dimension so revokes cause local misses rather than global evictions. Also quota per-tenant eviction to avoid snowballing OOMs.

mira: Agree. We'll also track hot-tenant scoreboard and evict least-recently-used tiles scoped by tenant quota.

devops-bot: scheduled canary job: dashboard-edge-auth-canary -> start 2023-11-09T09:00Z (pending security sign-off)

jose: I'll write the short RFC follow-up with measured numbers, rollout checklist, and security checklist. Target to start canary after sign-off. Any objections?

tara: No objections, please include cost delta estimate (cpu + network + key ops).

kevin: LGTM, add the chaos test and the tracing tags to the console spec PR.

jose: Thanks all, I'll post the follow-up link here once it's up.
